sources_read: rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx sheet1 row 45 (#44 dimension_and_criterion_weights_are_honest) and sheet4 row 45 incl. Mukesh annotation (functional 60%, per-dimension verifier weightage)
evidence: Dimension weights in task/tests/scoring.toml lines 5-11 are functional 0.6 / polish 0.2 / visual 0.2 with functional floor 0.05, byte-identical to the template scoring.toml and matching the workbook annotation (functional 60%) and SKILL.md line 28; gates are 0.0. score.py (identical to template) computes a weighted mean, so non-functional dimensions can contribute at most 0.4 and only once functional > 0.05. Functional criteria (judge.toml lines 38-292) sum to 42.0 as the comment claims; the instruction's two stated priorities get the heaviest weights: walls 10.0 (wall_every_route 4, wall_mentions_and_links 4, wall_added_live 2), retention 10.0 (deleted_and_expired_messages 4, timer_changes 4, hold_scope_and_release 2), client scope 3.0, persistence 2.0 (23-25 of 42), while ordinary chat behaviours sit at 1.5 each (nested_replies, safe_formatting, message_links, unread, live_updates) and composite chat criteria at 2.5-4.0 by part count. No structural or cosmetic check sits inside functional. Polish criteria are six equal 1.0 small behaviours; visual likert weights put the domain-relevant matter_sidebar and retention_marks (2.0) above transcript_page and phone_chambers (1.0). No criterion grading style or structure outweighs one grading real behaviour within its dimension, and no weight key appears in any [judge] block. Adversarial probes: (1) an app ignoring walls and retention entirely but doing all ordinary chat, sign-in/client scope, search/transcript and durability could pass ~22/42 functional, reward about 0.6*0.524+0.4=0.71, versus about 0.81 for a core-perfect app with weak chat at equal polish/visual - core still ranks higher and each core criterion outweighs each chat criterion, so the ordering is honest; (2) a minimal post/search/transcript app clearing the floor via sent_once_in_order (2.5/42=0.06) would be capped by polish/visual criteria that themselves require edits, deletes, holds and unread counts, and floor/dimension values are template-controlled. Minor non-blocking observation: the weight-rule comment (judge.toml lines 32-35) says single core criteria are 2.0 and multi-part criteria take sums, yet wall_every_route and timer_changes are 4.0 without Part labels (each defensibly bundles a read-leak plus a write/authorization observable) and signin_and_client_scope is 3.0 although client scope is confidentiality-grade; the values are defensible, only the comment's derivation is loose. Static review only; no judge run is needed or claimed for this row.
suggested_fix: Optional: reword the functional weight-rule comment so it explains the 4.0 single-block criteria (wall_every_route, timer_changes) and the 3.0 signin_and_client_scope split; no weight change required.
run_verdict: PASS (static review of frozen weights; no runtime measurement required for this row)
